headline: October hike 70.3% priced vs 17.7% a month ago, 50bp by December 54.8%
stance: Monday repriced the Fed, not the oil premium. October is a hike at 70%, and real yields did the work.

news.head: Saudi pipeline restart breaks Iran's grip on Hormuz
news.body: East-West flows to the Red Sea are back near 3.5m barrels a day. Regional exports hit the most since February.

news.head: Trump weighing a ban on diesel exports
news.body: Said Monday, with fuel prices climbing before the November midterms. It would cut refining-hub prices and lift jet fuel.

news.head: Gold fell 3.6% Monday, silver 5.8%
news.body: Gold closed at its weakest since early August. A higher policy path costs a non-yielding asset more.

news.head: RBA raised 25bp overnight
news.body: Australia joins the Fed in tightening again. Rate markets are pricing a faster global cycle than weeks ago.

implications: 50bp by December is now better than a coin flip. That is a discount-rate problem for equities, not an earnings one.
Oil supply is returning while the Fed is priced off oil. A Hormuz deal unwinds the rates move, not just the crude move.

watch.head: Job openings (JOLTS), 10:00
watch.body: August openings, forecast 7.23m against 7.271m in July. Three days before the payroll report.

watch.head: US response to Iran due today
watch.body: Qatar is relaying a revised proposal on reopening the strait. Tehran expects Washington's formal answer Tuesday.

watch.head: Six Fed speakers today
watch.body: First of 14 scheduled before Friday's payroll report.

watch.head: Core PCE, Sep 30, 8:30
watch.body: Forecast 0.3% on the month and 3.4% on the year, from 3.3%. It lands on quarter-end.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: Real yields drove the move, not breakevens. The 10y real yield closed at a post-2008 high Monday.
The 2y rose more than 50bp in September, its largest monthly move since February 2023.
Cook said Monday oil and AI demand keep inflation pressure coming. She did not commit to another hike.
sections.positioning: COT, Sep 22: specs moved the euro to the 13th percentile of 3 years, a new extended short this week.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Breadth broke down Monday. Decliners beat advancers 3.05-to-1 on the NYSE, and the Nasdaq had 215 new lows against 39 highs.
The 10y is up 28bp since Sep 9 and 37bp since Aug 21. Street work puts the equity stall point near 30bp in two weeks.
Futures mixed pre-market (~5am ET): Dow -0.16%, S&P 500 -0.03%, Nasdaq-100 +0.12%.
sections.positioning: COT, Sep 22: specs extended short VIX for a 7th week, 15th percentile of 3 years. Standing background, not new.

single_name.note: BCB Bancorp: two insider rules fired and it trades above its 200-day. New to the screen Monday, top score.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: The 7y auction last week stopped at 5.085%, a record for the tenor, with the weakest cover in a year. Foreign allocation fell with it.
Treasury bought back only $4.08bn of 20y-30y paper last week, against about $6bn expected.
Equity-credit correlation is 0.61. Credit still trades with stocks, so a rates-led selloff hits both.
